subject: Runway slate & capacity askboard — OKR check-in: GPU burn, batching & cache impact
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runway slate & capacity askboard — OKR check-in: GPU burn, batching & cache impact

Team —

Short note ahead of the OKR check-in tomorrow: leadership asked for a one-slide summary of runway sensitivity driven by our top three levers (GPU burn, utilization, and batching/KV cache effectiveness). I want to pull a concise askboard so we can defend the recommended slate during the QBR.

Asks: 
- Markus: can you share a 2x2 sensitivity (burn vs. utilization) and a short note on assumptions for slot sizing by model family? A spreadsheet with the base-case and +/-20% scenarios would be ideal.
- Marissa: can you run the latest batching sim (5ms vs 15ms tail) and kv-cache hit rates for the APAC regressions? Inject the results into the askboard.
- Karthik: partner/market angle — any procurement windows or marketplace credits we should expect in the next 90 days that affect runway?

I've included Sarah from NimbusHealth since they need visibility on our planned burst strategy for their Q4 pilot. Sarah — if the current bursts (described in the sheet) look risky for you, flag the constraint and we'll route around it.

Attachments: proposed-askboard.csv (blank template), slot_runway_modeling.xlsx (base assumptions).

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway slate & capacity askboard — OKR check-in: GPU burn, batching & cache impact

Lauren — sending the first pass. Key highlights (see slot_runway_modeling.xlsx attached):

- Base case (current utilization 62%, avg slot size 1.0): monthly GPU spend $1.2M; runway at current revenue cadence = 7.8 months.
- If utilization slips to 50% (same demand), burn increases ~14% due to smaller effective batch densities; runway drops to ~6.8 months.
- If we apply the batching/caching recommendations (continuous batching + aggressive prefix cache) we estimate a 9–12% token-cost reduction in gen-heavy workloads — modeled as a 7% net reduction in GPU minutes after factoring latency SLOs.

Assumptions summarized in the sheet: model mix (chat: 48%, embeddings: 22%, rerank: 8%, infrequent large-context: 22%), p50 sequence length 128, p95 512, average KV-cache hit 18% baseline.

Attachments: slot_runway_modeling.xlsx (sheets: base_case, scenario_minus20pct, scenario_plus20pct). Also exported a short PDF of the batching sim (batching-sim-results.pdf).

Markus
Director, Inference Runtime

Subject: Re: Runway slate & capacity askboard — OKR check-in: GPU burn, batching & cache impact

Adding the batching sim notes and the ASKBOARD CSV filled with prioritized asks. Short summary:

- Batching sims (attached PDF) show that moving from 5ms slot fill to a 15ms soft-latency budget increases effective batch size by ~26% for gen requests; tail latency p99 increases by ~0.9s for long-context tails in worst-case.
- KV-cache tweaks (prefix-only + cold-start pre-warm) improved hit rate from 18% -> 31% in our synthetic workload, which reduces end-to-end token compute by ~14% for cached flows. Net effect when both levers applied: ~18% GPU-minute savings for mixed traffic.
- Risk: some customer-facing SLOs could see higher p99 for long-context calls; recommended mitigation is route-by-policy for latency-sensitive customers and a fallback to pinned lower-latency instance types.

I've attached proposed-askboard.csv (filled) with owners and slotted impact buckets; see column H for expected runway delta.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Operations

Thanks for the visibility — the askboard and the sim notes are really helpful. A couple quick items from our side: 

- Nimbus is comfortable with an occasional burst to support the Q4 pilot if the expected p99 increases are isolated to long-context workflows. We do not want burst exposures to affect our SLA-backed features (real-time vitals); those must stay on low-latency routes.
- Procurement note: we have a conversation scheduled with GCP next week about committed-use discounts; if there is an opportunity to coordinate, happy to loop in Markus and Karthik.

I'll review the askboard and flag any schedule conflicts by EOD Thursday.

— Sarah
